2026-03-02.summary: The US and Israel struck Iran's Natanz nuclear enrichment complex, and Iran's IRGC announced the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting global shipping. Kuwait intercepted 178 ballistic missiles and 384 drones; the UAE intercepted 169 missiles and 645 drones, with 44 hitting Emirati territory.

2026-03-03.summary: Massive explosions were heard in Tehran, with blasts also reported in Karaj and Isfahan. Iran's IRGC announced that ground forces had entered battlefield operations, engaging 230 drones, and described a naval operation targeting US military ships.

2026-03-04.summary: Israel launched a new 'broad wave' of strikes targeting Iran's leadership and security command centers; Trump said Iran's air force and navy had been 'knocked out.' A US-based rights group said more than 1,000 people had been killed in Iran since the fighting began, and four US service members were killed in a drone strike in Kuwait.

2026-03-05.summary: Iran fired a hybrid drone-and-missile barrage at Tel Aviv, including what appeared to be a cluster warhead. Kuwait, Bahrain and the UAE faced a fresh barrage of Iranian attacks. Maersk suspended Middle East operations; US and Brent crude surged 31% and 24% respectively on the week as Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.

2026-03-06.summary: Trump warned Iran would be hit 'very hard' and that Washington would widen its target list; US Central Command said more than 3,000 targets inside Iran had been struck in the preceding week. Fresh drone and missile attacks hit Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain and the UAE, and Dubai's airport came under repeated drone attack.

2026-03-09.summary: More than a week after Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed in the February 28 strikes, Iran named his son Mojtaba Khamenei as successor; hundreds of thousands rallied in Tehran in support. Brent crude surged to $119.50/barrel before easing to $112.98. Trump said the war could be over 'pretty quickly.'

2026-03-24.summary: Trump said VP Vance and Secretary of State Rubio were leading negotiations with Iran and expressed optimism a deal was in sight; Iranian officials called the claims 'fake news' and a 'big lie,' accusing the US of buying time while deploying more forces. The Philippines declared a state of national emergency over energy-supply risk from the war.

2026-03-25.summary: Oil prices tumbled and stock markets rallied on reports of a US plan to end the war with Iran, which Tehran promptly rejected, saying Washington's push for talks alongside continued troop deployments showed a lack of genuine diplomatic intent. Iran reported more than 1,750 killed since the war began.

2026-03-26.summary: Trump said the US would hold off on targeting Iranian energy sites for 10 more days as 'talks are ongoing'; Iran's foreign minister acknowledged messages exchanged via mediators but called the shift in US tone an admission of failure. The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq were each set for their worst month in a year.

2026-03-30.summary: Trump said in an interview he wanted to 'take the oil in Iran' and threatened to obliterate Iran's electric plants and oil wells if a deal wasn't reached, even as he pushed publicly for negotiations. An Indian worker was killed in Kuwait; Iranian-backed Houthi rebels joined the conflict for the first time, and fears of a US ground invasion grew as troops arrived in the region.

2026-04-06.summary: Trump set an 8pm ET deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face strikes on power plants and bridges; a 45-day ceasefire proposal was rejected by both sides as insufficient. A US-Israeli strike near Tehran's Sharif University damaged a fuel station and mosque; children were reported killed in overnight strikes on a residential Tehran neighborhood.

2026-04-08.summary: The US and Iran agreed a two-week ceasefire brokered by Pakistan, ending 40 days of attacks, conditioned on Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Negotiations toward a lasting agreement were set to begin in Islamabad. Israel endorsed the ceasefire with Iran but said it would not extend to its operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon.

2026-04-09.summary: Iran's IRGC claimed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz stopped again over an alleged Israeli ceasefire violation in Lebanon, even as the US-Iran truce held elsewhere. Satellite imagery showed large plumes of black smoke over Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq processing facility following a reported Iranian strike the day before.

2026-04-10.summary: Trump said the Strait of Hormuz would reopen soon, 'with or without Iran's cooperation,' and threatened to renew and intensify strikes if a lasting deal wasn't reached. Polls found most Israelis did not believe the war had been won, and more than half opposed the ceasefire. A key Saudi pipeline bypassing the Strait was struck earlier that week.

2026-04-13.summary: A US military blockade of all traffic entering or leaving Iranian ports took effect at 10am ET, after weekend ceasefire talks in Pakistan collapsed. Iran's IRGC vowed to retaliate and warned that approaching military vessels would breach the ceasefire. Oil prices were expected to keep climbing until meaningful tanker traffic resumed through the Strait.

2026-06-15.summary: Oil sank after the US and Iran agreed an interim deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz ahead of a framework agreement to end the war; Brent tumbled as much as 5.7% to below $83/barrel, more than 30% off its wartime peak, as Iran prepared to end its near-total closure of the Strait in exchange for the US lifting its port blockade.

2026-07-08.summary: Iran warned of a 'crushing response' after US strikes 'punished' Iranian attacks on three commercial vessels near the Strait of Hormuz the day before; Iran's IRGC claimed strikes on 85 US targets across Bahrain and Kuwait. The June memorandum-of-understanding ceasefire was widely reported as effectively over.

2026-07-13.summary: The US resumed strikes on Iran for a second consecutive night, hitting air-defense systems, coastal radar sites and missile/drone capabilities; Iran said it struck and disabled two 'rogue supertankers' and hit US-linked facilities in Bahrain, Oman, Jordan and Kuwait. WTI rose 9.4% to $78.14/barrel, its highest settle since June 15. US Central Command said it would resume its naval blockade of Iranian ports the next day.
